# certloom_endpoint (Resource)

A TLS endpoint certloom probes on a schedule. Each probe records the served chain and raises findings (expiry, hostname mismatch, weak keys, chain problems). Host, port and SNI identify the endpoint; changing them replaces it. Deleting an endpoint resolves its open findings.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "certloom_endpoint" "portal" {
  host             = "portal.corp.example.com"
  scope_id         = certloom_scope.internal.id
  team_id          = certloom_team.platform.id
  interval_seconds = 3600
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `host` (String) Host name or IP address to connect to.
- `scope_id` (String) Probe scope (`certloom_scope.<name>.id`). The scope must allow the host and port.

### Optional

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the endpoint is probed.
- `interval_seconds` (Number) Seconds between probes. Defaults to six hours.
- `lineage_id` (String) Lineage the endpoint is expected to serve.
- `port` (Number) TCP port.
- `sni` (String) Server name to send in the TLS handshake when it differs from `host`.
- `team_id` (String) Owning team (`certloom_team.<name>.id`).

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier assigned by certloom.
- `version` (Number) Configuration version. Updates are sent with `If-Match`, so a change made outside Terraform since the last refresh fails the apply instead of being overwritten.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by id, as shown by the certloom CLI or API.
terraform import certloom_endpoint.example <id>
```
